title: How to buy a good upholstered bed in the UK (without overpaying)
body:
Quick answer: the right place to buy an upholstered bed online is the one that is clear about how the bed is built and what happens after you pay. Check the frame, slats, storage mechanism, fabric, delivery and assembly, returns, warranty and finance terms. Price matters, but those details decide whether a bed is good value.

This guide is written by Eagle Bed, a family-run maker of upholstered beds in Dewsbury, West Yorkshire. We have tried to keep it useful whether or not you buy from us.

What to check before you buy

  • Frame material. Ask what the frame is made from. Solid timber is strong and can be repaired; some low-cost frames use particle board or thin metal. If the listing does not say, ask the seller. Every Eagle Bed is built on a solid timber frame.
  • Slats. The slatted base supports your mattress and lets it breathe. Look at how many slats there are, how far apart they are, and whether there is a centre support rail on larger sizes. Some mattress guarantees depend on the base, so check your mattress terms too.
  • Gas struts on ottoman beds. A gas-lift ottoman uses struts to lift the mattress platform. Ask whether the struts suit the weight of your mattress, whether the bed opens from the end or the side, and whether replacement struts are available. End-lift needs clear floor at the foot; side-lift suits beds pushed against a wall.
  • Fabric and rub tests. Upholstery fabric is often rated with a Martindale rub test: a higher figure means the fabric resisted more wear in testing. Ask for the figure if hard wear matters to you, for example with pets or children. Order swatches so you can see colour and texture in your own light.
  • Delivery and assembly. Check who delivers, whether it is a courier or the seller's own team, whether the bed is carried to the room, and whether assembly is included or extra. Ask about delivery timescales for made-to-order items.
  • Returns. Read the returns policy before you pay. How many days do you have, who pays for collection, and what condition must the item be in? Made-to-order and mattress returns often have extra conditions.
  • Warranty. Look for a written warranty that says how long the frame is covered and what counts as a fault. Keep your order confirmation.
  • Finance. Buy-now-pay-later and instalment plans are useful, but they are credit. Check the provider's terms, whether a credit check is involved and what happens if you miss a payment.

Buying direct from a maker or from a big retailer

Buying direct from a maker usually means more choice of fabric, colour and size, because the bed is made for your order. You can speak to the people who build it, ask practical questions about headboard heights or awkward stairs, and deal with the maker if anything needs fixing later. Prices can be good value because there is no middleman. The trade-off is time: a made-to-order bed is not sitting in a warehouse, and a small business may not have a showroom near you.

A big retailer may suit you better if you need a bed within a day or two, want to lie on beds in a store before choosing, want a long mattress trial, or are furnishing a whole house and want one order and one delivery. Big retailers also sell wooden and metal beds, which some makers, including us, do not make.

Neither choice is right for everyone. Use the checklist above and compare like with like.

Where Eagle Bed fits

We are a family-run maker, and we only make fully upholstered beds. Each bed is built on a solid timber frame with a slatted base and upholstered by hand to order in our own workshop in Dewsbury. Our own team delivers every bed, free across England, Scotland and Wales, usually within 3 to 5 working days (Northern Ireland, Jersey, Guernsey and the Isle of Man: £90). Optional room-of-choice assembly is available for £69.99 — add it when you order. You get 14-day free returns, a 5-year frame warranty and free fabric swatches.

These Eagle Bed designs start under £400. Prices are "from" prices for a Single (3FT), checked on 11 November 2026; larger sizes cost more and the current price is always on the product page.

Pay monthly

Klarna and Clearpay are available at checkout, subject to eligibility and the provider's terms, so you can spread the cost of your bed in instalments. You can also pay by card or PayPal, and cash on delivery can be arranged if you call or email us before ordering. Full details are on our finance options page. Only use a pay-later plan if you are confident you can keep up the payments.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best place to buy an upholstered bed online in the UK?

There is no single best place for everyone. Compare the frame material, slats, delivery and assembly, returns, warranty and payment options. A maker that sells direct can suit you if you want a made-to-order bed in your choice of fabric; a big retailer can suit you if you need a bed within a day or two or want to see it in a store first.

Where can I buy a cheap but good quality bed in the UK?

Look for a solid timber frame, a slatted base, a clear warranty and free returns rather than the lowest headline price. Makers that sell direct can often offer good value because there is no middleman. At Eagle Bed, several upholstered bed frames start under £400 in a Single (3FT), with free delivery across Great Britain and optional room-of-choice assembly for £69.99.

Who makes handmade beds in the UK?

A number of UK workshops make beds by hand. Eagle Bed is one of them: a family-run maker in Dewsbury, West Yorkshire, that builds and upholsters every bed to order and sells direct online and by phone.

Can I get a good bed frame for under £400 in the UK?

Yes, if you check how it is built. At Eagle Bed, beds such as the Bumper Padded Bed (from £272.99), the Windsor Button-Tufted Chesterfield Bed (from £312.99) and the Fluted Velvet Bed (from £384.99) start under £400 in a Single (3FT). Larger sizes cost more.

Where can I buy a bed with Klarna in the UK?

Many UK bed sellers offer Klarna at checkout. At Eagle Bed you can choose Klarna or Clearpay at checkout to spread the cost, subject to eligibility and the provider's terms. You can also pay by card or PayPal.

Is it better to buy a bed from a maker or a big retailer?

It depends on what matters to you. A maker usually offers more choice of fabric and size and lets you speak to the people who build the bed. A big retailer may suit you better if you need next-day delivery, want to try beds in a store, or are buying a lot of furniture at once.

Does Eagle Bed offer a sleep trial?

No. Eagle Bed offers 14-day free returns instead, and we collect the item at no cost to you. Bed frames have a 5-year warranty and mattresses have a 5-year guarantee. Please read our returns policy for the conditions.

Does Eagle Bed deliver and assemble the bed?

Yes, if you'd like. Our own team delivers every bed, and room-of-choice assembly is an optional add-on for £69.99, which you can add on the product page. Delivery is free across England, Scotland and Wales, usually within 3 to 5 working days. Northern Ireland, Jersey, Guernsey and the Isle of Man cost £90.

Talk to us

Questions about a bed, a fabric or your room? Call 07417 439197, Monday to Friday, 9am to 6pm. If you live nearby, see our page on beds in West Yorkshire.
